t: Count Houses in a Circular Street
o: We stand before one door of an unknown-length circular street (at most k houses) and must count houses using only the Street API. Doors start in an arbitrary open/closed state, so we cannot simply walk until we see an open door. Trick: first normalize by walking k houses and closing every open door; then open the current door and walk right until we hit an open door again — the number of steps equals the house count, since we will come back around to the only open door.
k: With n ≤ k steps you can force every door closed regardless of initial state.
After opening exactly one door, walking right until it reappears takes exactly n steps.

a.i: Close all doors in k steps to erase initial state, open the starting door, then count moves until an open door is found. That open door is necessarily the one we opened, so the move count is n.
s: Loop k times: close the door if open, then moveRight.
Move right, incrementing a counter, until isDoorOpen() is true; return the counter.
a.t: O(k) — one normalization pass plus at most n ≤ k probe steps

w: Always normalize state before probing on interactive problems with unknown initial conditions. Pitfall: forgetting that doors may start open, or stopping the probe loop too early. Follow-up: minimize the number of API calls (this solution is already asymptotically optimal at ~2k calls).
